title: Binary Tree Right Side View
description:
# Binary Tree Right Side View

Given the `root` of a binary tree, imagine yourself standing on the **right side** of it, return *the values of the nodes you can see ordered from top to bottom*.

## Example 1:

**Input:** root = [1,2,3,null,5,null,4]
**Output:** [1,3,4]

## Example 2:

**Input:** root = [1,null,3]
**Output:** [1,3]

## Example 3:

**Input:** root = []
**Output:** []

## Constraints:

*   The number of nodes in the tree is in the range `[0, 100]`.
*   `-100 <= Node.val <= 100`

solutions.name: BFS - Last Node per Level
solutions.description: Use BFS level-order traversal. The last node processed at each level is visible from the right side.

solutions.name: DFS - Right First
solutions.description: DFS visiting right child first. The first node visited at each depth level is the rightmost node.
